title: Measure what a re-encode above 1080 lines costs, and how often a viewer gets a capped one
description: Serves "The picture is as good as the device and the connection allow."; "The picture follows the connection.". Every re-encode is H.264 SDR at no more than 1080 lines (DOMAINS 41, for cost). No decision accepted that ceiling, and the cost of keeping a 4K film's height or an HDR film's range in a re-encode is unmeasured: JS-135 measures 4K sources, not 2160-line outputs. A viewer on a 4K or HDR screen whose film must be re-encoded (a burned-in PGS track on a 4K Blu-ray rip included) sees 1080p SDR.
acceptanceCriteria: Measured through a worker's own command with the 1080 limit lifted for the measurement only, from a 4K real-film source, SDR and HDR, on ffmpeg 6.1 and ffmpeg 9, on 2, 4 and 8 CPUs: H.264 at 1440 and 2160 lines at veryfast and faster, and 10-bit HEVC at 1080 and 2160 lines with the range kept. For each: CPU seconds per second of film, time to the first and the fourth segment, and whether it holds 1.2 times real time alone and with helpers
The HEVC fallback's 1080p and 4K prices are measured on the same real film, and Spec.Cost's rows are raised where found low
Whether Octave's players (Media3 on Android TV, and the browser) play H.264 at 2160 lines without stalling is observed

From JS-153's decision line and counter on the dogfood over at least 14 days, counts only, no titles: re-encodes started; how many had a source above 1080 lines and a client and cap that would have taken more; how many were HDR sources sent to a client that declares HDR; each split by reason (codec, quality cap, burned-in subtitle)
Recorded in docs/transcoding.md with machine and command

The figures go to the product owner as a brief with keeping the source's height and range priced per viewer, on CPU and on a GPU family; its decision names the task that closes the gap or accepts it, and docs/status.md's line is updated; its GPU figure is JS-163's (the HD 530 neither decodes Main 10 nor tone maps, JS-154), or is stated unmeasured if JS-163 has not run, and today's 2160-to-1080 burn-in path is measured there, not here
